Imaging Sensor.name: Silicon
Imaging Sensor.reasoning: Silicon is the fundamental semiconductor material for imaging sensors, essential for photodiode arrays and charge-coupled devices with no commercial alternatives.

Imaging Sensor.name: Gallium arsenide
Imaging Sensor.reasoning: Used in some advanced imaging sensors for infrared detection due to superior electronic and optical properties, though silicon sensors are more common.

Imaging Sensor.name: Indium gallium arsenide
Imaging Sensor.reasoning: Employed in infrared sensors for high sensitivity, especially in night vision, but less common than silicon or gallium arsenide; alternatives exist.

Imaging Sensor.name: Aluminum oxide
Imaging Sensor.reasoning: Used as insulating and passivation layers in sensor chips, commonly applied but other oxides can sometimes substitute.

Imaging Sensor.name: Copper
Imaging Sensor.reasoning: Copper is the standard conductor material for interconnects in imaging sensors, critical for electrical connections.

Objective Lens.name: Glass
Objective Lens.reasoning: Glass is the primary transparent material for objective lenses offering optical clarity and durability, standard in optics manufacturing.

Objective Lens.name: Borosilicate glass
Objective Lens.reasoning: Sometimes used due to its thermal and chemical stability for lenses subjected to variable conditions, though standard glass is more typical.

Objective Lens.name: Germanium
Objective Lens.reasoning: Germanium is widely used in infrared optics for night vision lenses due to its IR transparency, crucial for infrared transmission in this application.

Objective Lens.name: Silicon dioxide
Objective Lens.reasoning: Common as an anti-reflective coating and surface layer on lenses to improve optical performance.

Objective Lens.name: Aluminum
Objective Lens.reasoning: Used in lens mounts or as reflective coatings in some optical systems, though alternative metals also used.
